intent.subtype: unique case on 1'b1 whose items can overlap depending on an input
intent.rationale: If req is not one-hot, two items match and unique is violated; the input has no stated range.

labels.note: unique case (1'b1) over req bits that may be set together (lowest index serviced first) overlaps, violating unique and letting synthesis drop the priority.
unique case(1'b1) on req whose bits may be set together violates uniqueness; the lowest-index priority described needs priority/if-else, synthesis may build a parallel OR mux.

settlement.note: unique case (1'b1) items overlap only when req is not one-hot; req is an unconstrained input port and the question is a one-hot value assumption, so the file cannot decide (convention 2).
